definition.text: Catalysis of the reaction: 2'-deoxyadenosine + H+ + H2O = 2'-deoxyinosine + NH4+.
Catalysis of the reaction: 5'-deoxyadenosine + H2O + H+ = 5'-deoxyinosine + NH4+.
The chemical reactions and pathways involving deoxyadenosine, 2-deoxyribosyladenine, one of the four major nucleosides of DNA.
Catalysis of the reaction: 2'-deoxyadenosine + ATP = ADP + dAMP + 2 H+.
The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the breakdown of deoxyadenosine, 2-deoxyribosyladenine, one of the four major nucleosides of DNA.
The chemical reactions and pathways resulting in the formation of deoxyadenosine, 2-deoxyribosyladenine, one of the four major nucleosides of DNA.
Binding to an enzyme that catalyzes the removal of an amino group from a substrate, producing ammonia (NH3).
Catalysis of the removal of an amino group from a substrate, producing a substituted or nonsubstituted ammonia (NH4+/NH2R).
Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a cordycepin stimulus.
Catalysis of the reaction: 3',5'-cyclic AMP + H2O + H+ = 3',5'-cyclic IMP + NH4+.
Catalysis of the reaction: adenosine + H2O = inosine + NH4+.
Catalysis of the reaction: 7,8-dihydropterin + H2O = 7,8-dihydrolumazine + NH4+.
Catalysis of the reaction: cytidine + H+ + H2O = uridine + NH4 and deoxycytidine + H+ + H2O = deoxyuridine + NH4+.
Catalysis of the reaction: cytosine + H2O = uracil + NH4+.
Catalysis of the reaction: dCMP + H2O = dUMP + NH4+.
